subject.title: [Bug]: One-shot run cleanup leaks codex app-server process (inverted closeAndWait condition) → duplicate app-servers → spurious turn_aborted

question: Should this be fixed now as the unclaimed/idle one-shot cleanup gap, or should it first be folded into the broader shared-client lifecycle work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99947?
rationale: The report has strong field evidence, but current source contradicts part of the proposed root cause, so maintainer intent is needed before automation changes a concurrency-sensitive Codex cleanup path.

options.title: Require Focused Current-Main Proof
options.body: Run or request a current-main macOS/gateway repro that counts `codex app-server --listen stdio://` children before choosing the repair shape.

options.title: Patch Narrow Unclaimed Cleanup
options.body: Treat the report as sufficient and patch only the case where one-shot cleanup owns a client that `retireSharedCodexAppServerClientIfCurrent` does not match.

options.title: Fold Into Shared-Client Lifecycle Work
options.body: Keep this issue linked as evidence while resolving the active-lease and fallback concerns under the broader Codex cleanup cluster.

recommendation.title: Require Focused Current-Main Proof
recommendation.body: Run or request a current-main macOS/gateway repro that counts `codex app-server --listen stdio://` children before choosing the repair shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent current-main blame and shared-client startup cleanup history point to this owner for deciding whether the current condition is a real leak or an incomplete root-cause theory.
